note: Rounding::Down on both mint and redeem legs guarantees tok_out <= amount_in. No value created by rounding.

invariant: pool and issuance non-negative after redeem
note: Python flagged negative values; Rust uses checked_sub -> Err(CalculationOverflow) which aborts the transaction. No underflow in practice.
Floor rounding preserves weak monotonicity for sequential inputs at fixed pool/issuance.

invariant: tok_out <= net_in (no rounding gain on round-trip)
note: Double Rounding::Down ensures round-trip never gains; small losses possible.

invariant: mint fee deduction: net = gross - floor(rate * gross) is correct
note: Permill::mul_floor on fee amount, then subtract. Matches spec. mul_floor on fee = ceil on net (slightly more conservative, less risk of value creation).

invariant: impl(x) == spec(x): vout = floor(net_in * issuance / pool)
note: multiply_by_rational_with_rounding(net_in, issuance, pool, Down) matches floor(a*b/c) exactly.

invariant: impl(x) == spec(x): token_out = floor(net_v * pool / issuance)
note: multiply_by_rational_with_rounding(net_v, pool, issuance, Down) matches spec.
Each mint calls update_pool_and_issuance with +v_currency_amount adjustment. Sequential mints keep VtokenIssuance consistent.
adjustment=-(net_v) passed to update_pool_and_issuance. Sequential redeems keep VtokenIssuance consistent.
Redeem fee taken in vtokens (floor), then token_out computed on net_v. No value created at 1:1 rate.
Unlock ledger reduced by gross; pool increased by net. Delta = -fee. Fee properly transferred to FeeAccount.
Floor on rate_change_ppm means very slightly above limit could pass. < 0.0001% error. Conservative safety guard, not exploitable.

invariant: VtokenIssuance override changes exchange rate vs actual supply
note: Admin-only (root) set_v_currency_issuance is intentional for cross-chain burn reconciliation. Trust assumption documented.

No guard on vout==0 after get_v_currency_amount_by_currency_amount. If pool is seeded with 1 token (issuance=1) then a large staking-reward injection via increase_token_pool makes pool >> issuance. Any victim minting V < pool gets 0 vtokens: floor(V * 1 / pool) = 0. mint_into(0) is a no-op in Substrate fungibles; victim's tokens are deposited to entrance_account and pool grows but they receive nothing. MinimumMint only guards currency_amount >= min_amount, NOT vout >= 1. Attack path: SLP pallet injects first staking reward before any minter establishes a large pool. NOT fully permissionless (requires SLP timing) but a latent hazard during bootstrap. Fix: assert v_currency_amount > 0 before mint_into, or guard vout == 0 and revert.

get_v_currency_amount_by_currency_amount checks only pool==0, not issuance==0. If TokenPool==0 but VtokenIssuance>0 (broken state from admin ops or SLP miscalculation), new minter receives vtokens 1:1 as if bootstrapping, while existing holders have zero token backing. New minter dilutes existing holders severely. Guard should be: if pool==0 { if issuance>0 { return Err } else { return currency_amount } }. Reachable via: set_v_currency_issuance(positive) without touching pool, or SLP calling decrease_token_pool(full amount) while vtokens remain.

invariant: zero period-start snapshot blocks all mint/redeem operations
note: When ExchangeRateCheck is enabled on a fresh (empty) pool, update_exchange_rate_snapshot stores {pool:0, issuance:0}. Any subsequent mint attempt passes would-be pool>0 and issuance>0 to calculate_rate_change(start=0,0, current>0,>0) which returns None, blocking the operation. Operational DoS: admin must disable check, let pool initialize, re-enable. Fix: in calculate_rate_change, if start snapshot is zero return Permill::zero() (no change from baseline, not block). Or skip check when snapshot is (0,0).
